paragraphs: The son of Rabbi Chinena; see the entry "Bar Yeshita."

notes.text: The notice calls Yeshita the son of Rabbi Chinena, but points to “Bar Yeshita.” The direction of this relationship needs checking against the source.

The earlier local note’s inference that the pointer necessarily reverses the relationship is qualified: the saved local V42 Bar Yeshita notice itself describes the subject as Abbahu’s amora and Chinena’s son. Hyman’s two notices can therefore be compared without treating the name Bar Yeshita as a separately established fatherhood claim. This is internal textual evidence, not independent genealogy verification; the source hold remains.

The printed Yeshita entry (Hyman, vol. II, p. 817) points to Bar Yeshita, whose printed entry (vol. I, p. 286) also identifies Rabbi Chinena as his father and calls him Rabbi Abbahu’s interpreter. Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:10 reads Abbahu, while the Guggenheimer text reads Rabbi Acha. That text distinguishes what Bar Yeshita heard from his father from what he reports in Rabbi Chinena’s name. Hyman’s cross-reference and identification are preserved as his account. The reference to a source hold in the preceding note records the earlier stage of this review.
